# z-serial frame vectors, written by `z-serial` 0.2.3 itself.
#
# `zenoh-link-serial` 1.0.0 puts every message on the line as one z-serial frame: a COBS body ended by the sentinel 0x00. The
# body is a 2-byte little-endian length, the data, and a 4-byte little-endian CRC. The CRC is not the standard CRC-32: it is
# the polynomial 0x04C11DB7 in a reflected loop with an inverted accumulator.
#
# Source: crates.io `z-serial` 0.2.3, SHA-256 f113597c6b880587004169f14bc010e4b440981ab2ad669779d3654f9b1c4af1. The frames
# are what `WireFormat::serialize_into` wrote. The decode lines are what `WireFormat::deserialize_into` did with each wire.
# An empty payload is written '-'. A decode result is `ok <data hex>` or `refused`.
#
#   frame  <name> <data hex> <wire hex>      what the stock writer produced
#   decode <name> <wire hex> ok <data hex>   a wire the stock reader accepted, and the data it returned
#   decode <name> <wire hex> refused         a wire the stock reader refused
#   limit  <name> <data length> <result>     the stock writer on an over-long payload
